news.title: Lego sales jump 21% to nearly £5bn, helped by World Cup and F1 ranges
news.lede: Lego sales have risen by more than a fifth as tie-ups with the football World Cup, Formula One and the hit film KPop Demon Hunters as well as its flower-based and Star Wars kits drive demand. The toymaker said its revenues had increased by 21% to 41.9bn Danish kroner (£4.8bn) in the first six months of 2026, driven by strong growth in the Americas, Europe and the Asia-Pacific regions, offsetting stalled sales in China. Sales by its clients to consumers rose by 22% as it produced World Cup kits, including mini figures of players such as Harry Kane and even building kits of superstar players, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi which were retailing for up to £159.99. Net profit increased 32% to 8.6bn Danish kroner (£1bn) as the group launched 330 new products including its hi-tech Smart Play kit, with bricks that emit sounds and light.

news.title: John Swinney launches £500k World Cup fund to 'back Scotland's future football stars'
news.lede: JOHN Swinney has launched a £500,000 World Cup fund to "support Scotland's future football stars". The First Minister launched the fund during a visit to Scotland's national stadium, Hampden Park in Glasgow, on Tuesday. It comes following the success of Steve Clarke's team at the Fifa World Cup in June, with the Scotland men's team qualifying for the tournament for the first time since 1998. Lawrence Shankland celebrates during win over Denmark at Hampden Park in November, in which Scotland qualified for the World Cup (Image: PA).

news.title: Three World Cup winners buy own top flight club for just £34m in huge investment
news.lede: THREE World Cup winners are part of an investment group that has bought a 90 per cent stake in Portuguese top-flight club Estrela da Amadora. Thomas Muller, Mats Hummels and Lucas Hernandez are among the football stars involved in the takeover, alongside former Bayern Munich goalkeeper Yann Sommer. The German-led consortium has completed a deal worth around £34million to acquire the majority stake in the Lisbon-based club’s professional football operation. The deal was officially confirmed by Estrela on Tuesday, with the consortium led by ADvantage and LEAD, backed by the KI Group.

news.title: Iraq Retains Graham Arnold After Historic World Cup Return
news.lede: Graham Arnold has extended his Iraq coaching contract through the 2027 Asian Cup after guiding the Iraqi national team back to the World Cup after 40 years. ERBIL (Kurdistan24) - Graham Arnold has extended his contract as Iraq's national football coach through the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, choosing a six-month renewal after guiding the country back to the FIFA World Cup for the first time in four decades. The 63-year-old former Australia coach said the Iraq Football Association had offered him a four-year agreement, but he opted for the shorter extension as the national team turns its attention from this summer's World Cup to the Gulf Cup and Asian Cup. "I have renewed my contract for six months and this decision is in my best interest and in the best interest of the Iraq national team," Arnold told a news conference in Baghdad on Monday, according to The Associated Press.

news.title: World Cup ranges help drive record first half for Lego
news.lede: World Cup and KPop Demon Hunters ranges have helped toy giant Lego drive sales up by more than a fifth to hit another record in the first half of 2026. The Danish firm reported a 21% rise in revenues to 41.9 billion Danish kroner (£4.8 billion) for the six months to June 30, helping pre-tax profits surge a third higher to 11.3 billion Danish kroner (£1.3 billion). It launched more than 330 new products over the first half, with World Cup football fever and “consumer excitement” around Formula 1 and Netflix smash-hit movie KPop Demon Hunters drawing in new customers. New products included a replica of the official Fifa World Cup trophy, as well as new sets using interactive bricks, which have so far featured in Star Wars and Pokemon ranges.

news.title: World Cup cult hero Orlando Gill joins Lille to bolster Ancelotti's squad
news.lede: Securing the goalkeeperAccording to TyC Sports, Lille have completed the signing of Paraguay goalkeeper Orlando Gill from Argentine club San Lorenzo. The transfer fee is set at around €3.8 million, which covers 50% of his economic rights and provides a welcome financial boost to San Lorenzo. The 26-year-old shot-stopper made it clear he wanted to move to France, actively pushing his former club to accept the proposal from the Ligue 1 side after turning down an offer from Monza. During the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Gill emerged as a cult hero by saving two penalties in a dramatic shootout against Germany to help Paraguay reach the round of 16.

news.title: Tottenham have lost the plot! Spurs spending £85m on Savinho is one of the most ridiculous deals in football history : GOAL grades the biggest deals of the 2026 summer transfer window
news.lede: For some football fans, the summer is the part of the calendar that they look forward to the most - and that's not just because it's filled by a World Cup every four years! Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window is once again proving to be busy, with some huge names making big-money moves before deadline day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino seeks support from smaller nations
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has called for greater support for smaller football nations after meeting representatives of the Caribbean Football Union in the Dominican Republic. The Italian-Swiss leader wants to reduce the gap between the world’s biggest football countries and less powerful federations. “Some, unfortunately, don’t need or want others to grow, but we must reduce this gap between the big countries, the very big countries, and everyone else,” Infantino said, according to Marca. Infantino also defended greater investment in football development across the world.
